# Independent verification disposition

| Requirement | Disposition | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| R1 measured effects with conditions and cost where available | **Qualified** | Retained units give source-bound outcomes across search, long context, repair, retrieval, and tool loops. Only ToT reports token and historical dollar costs. |
| R2 counterevidence, regressions, transfer limits | **Supported** | Retained sources establish task/model dependence, end-position regressions, weak self-verification, retrieval bottlenecks, and benchmark-transfer limits. |
| R3 selection rules, failure signals, paired local evaluation | **Supported** | Streams provide concrete bounded artifacts and stage/final-state metrics. Product thresholds remain intentionally unspecified. |

## Retention units

| ID | Decision dimension | Source identity / URL | Exact result and units | Locator | Model, task, intervention, comparator, method | Caveat | Required report contribution | Source-unique | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1 | Search reasoning correctness versus cost | Yao et al., [Tree of Thoughts](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.10601) | Game of 24: ToT **74%** success, CoT **4.0%**, best-of-100 CoT **49%**. ToT **5.5k completion / 1.4k prompt tokens**, **$0.74** historical cost. | §4.1, App. B.3, Table 7 | GPT-4, 100 hard Game-of-24 items. BFS ToT, breadth 5, versus IO, CoT, CoT-SC, and best-of-100 CoT. | 2023 pricing, no latency or total operating cost. | Conditional bounded-search option for discrete, externally verifiable reasoning. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U2 | Subjective-text quality versus search/refinement cost | [Tree of Thoughts](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.10601) | ToT coherence **7.56** versus IO **6.19** and CoT **6.93** on 1–10 GPT-4 scale. Human preference: ToT **41/100**, CoT **21/100**, tie **38/100**. Refinement: IO **7.67**, ToT **7.91**. ToT **$0.32/task**, **4k / 2.9k completion/prompt tokens**. | §4.2, App. B.3, Table 8 | GPT-4 constrained writing, five plans/passages/votes versus IO and CoT. | LLM judging and small author-only human study limit transfer. | Do not present tree search as the default for subjective text. Test refinement and blinded domain evaluation. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |
| U3 | ToT model portability | [Tree of Thoughts](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.10601) | Game of 24 ToT: GPT-3.5 **19%** versus GPT-4 **74%**. GPT-4 generation/GPT-3.5 evaluation **64%**. GPT-3.5 generation/GPT-4 evaluation **31%**. | App. B.2 | Same ToT task with generation/evaluation model swaps. | Narrow task and prompt change for GPT-3.5. | Require target-model paired testing before adopting search scaffolds. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U4 | Long-context quote scratchpad and examples | Anthropic, [Prompt engineering for Claude’s long context window](https://www.anthropic.com/news/prompting-long-context) | Claude 2 baseline **0.939** to prompted **0.961** accuracy, stated as **36% error reduction**. Quote scratchpad helped all reported head-to-head comparisons, with small latency cost. | Evaluation and Results | Claude Instant 1.2 primary study, Claude 2 limited comparison. Synthetic government-document MCQ collages at 70K/95K tokens, answer location varied. | Vendor study, synthetic task, source-only failures excluded, chart cells not text-exposed. | Test quote extraction at production context length and answer position. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |
| U5 | End-position long-context regression | [Anthropic long-context study](https://www.anthropic.com/news/prompting-long-context) | Scratchpad/examples substantially improved beginning/middle performance but **can degrade** end-position performance. | Results notes | Same intervention and context-location experiment as U4. | No numeric end-position delta in accessible text. | Require position-stratified evaluation, not aggregate recall alone. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |
| U6 | Many-shot example-selection value and computational burden | Baek, Lee, Gupta, [Revisiting ICL with Long Context LMs](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.16926) | Across **18 datasets** and four task families, advanced selection was statistically significant over random in **fewer than 15%** of instances. | Abstract, §2.2–2.3, Table 2 | Gemini 1.5 Flash/Pro and Llama 3.1 70B. Random demonstrations versus relevance, diversity, curriculum, and hard-example selection. | Many-shot ICL, not quote extraction. Exact billing absent. | Compare query-selected examples against fixed cacheable examples under equal budgets. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U7 | Verifier-feedback modality and iteration limit | [FeedbackEval](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.06939) | Repair@1: mixed **63.6%**, LLM-Expert **62.9%**, test **57.9%**, minimal **53.1%**, compiler **49.2%**, LLM-Skilled **48.8%**. Marginal gain declines after **two or three iterations**. | Abstract, §4.2, §6 | GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, DeepSeek-R1, GLM-4, Qwen2.5 on code repair with six feedback types. | Aggregate benchmark result, not a no-feedback baseline. LLM-Expert uses ground-truth knowledge. | Prefer executable/structured diagnostics and cap repair loops. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |
| U8 | Same-model self-verification regression | Stechly et al., [Self-Verification Limitations](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.08115v2) | Across almost all domains, same-model self-verification **worsens performance**. More backprompts **consistently degrade** output quality. | Abstract; §5 | GPT-4 generates, critiques, and backprompts itself versus non-self-corrected generation. | Accessible support does not supply a single numerical aggregate delta. | Do not automate critique-and-rewrite absent a calibrated or executable verifier. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |
| U9 | Tool-call stage correctness | Li et al., [API-Bank](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.08244) | GPT-4: Call **63.66%**, Retrieve+Call **37.04%**, Plan+Retrieve+Call **70.00%**, total **60.24%** execution-equivalence correctness. GPT-4 errors: failed retrieval **67.86%**, false call format **17.86%**. | Table 3, Table 6, §§2.1, 3.3, 5 | `gpt-4-0613`; 73 APIs, 314 dialogues, 753 calls. Execution-equivalent effects, not syntax-only grading. | Fixed simulated APIs and small 50-instance advanced-condition subsets. | Separate retrieval, schema validity, execution effect, and task-success denominators. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U10 | Tool retrieval quality at catalog scale | Shi et al., [ToolRet](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.01763) | NV-Embed-v1: **nDCG@10 33.83**, **Completeness@10 32.12**. | Tables 1–2, §6 | Retrieval over **43,215 tools** and **7,615 tasks**. Completeness requires every required tool in top 10. | Aggregated datasets and potentially incomplete one-to-many labels. | Treat retrieval/reranking as a separately measured prerequisite to calling. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U11 | Retrieved-tool end-to-end loss | [ToolRet](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.01763) | **Corrected source result:** GPT-3.5 ToolBench-G1 pass rate **50.60** with `bge-large` retrieved tools, a **11.40-point decrease** from oracle candidates. | §7.1, Figure 5 | Retrieved candidate set versus annotated/oracle toolset. | ToolBench-specific retrieval-then-calling setup. Stream incorrectly attributes this result to ToolLlama. | Preserve only with corrected model identity and comparator. | Yes | **Reject as written; retain corrected unit** |
| U12 | Interactive agent benefit | Yao et al., [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.03629) | ALFWorld best trial: ReAct **71%**, Act **45%**, BUTLER **37%**. WebShop: ReAct **40.0%** success versus Act **30.1%**. | §4, Tables 3–4 | PaLM-540B few-shot trajectories, simulated interactive environments. | ALFWorld result is best-of-six, not average production performance. | Trial bounded observe–act loops only where observations/tool state resolve uncertainty. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |
| U13 | ReAct task dependence and fallback | [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.03629) | HotpotQA EM: ReAct **27.4**, CoT **29.4**, CoT-SC **33.4**. FEVER accuracy: ReAct **60.9%**, CoT **56.3%**, CoT-SC **60.4%**. Hybrid results: **35.1 EM** and **64.6%**. | Table 1, §3.3 | PaLM-540B with constrained Wikipedia search/lookup and few-shot prompts. | Not current tool APIs or production tasks. | Reject universal ReAct ranking. Use task-specific fallback/routing evaluation. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U14 | ReAct failure boundaries and unmeasured cost | [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.03629) | Sampled HotpotQA ReAct failures: reasoning **47%**, search-result **23%**, hallucination **0%**, label ambiguity **29%**. | Table 2, §3.3 | Human review of sampled trajectories. | Categories are within sampled failures, not benchmark-wide rates. No token, latency, call-count, or dollar result. | Instrument no-progress, failed retrieval, repeated action, and budget exhaustion locally. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |
| U15 | Tool-call trigger sensitivity | Schick et al., [Toolformer](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.04761) | Raising API-token top-*k* from 1 to 10 changes API-call rates from **40.3% to 98.1%** on T-REx and **8.5% to 100%** on WebQS. | §5, Table 9 | Toolformer, GPT-J 6.7B, decoding-policy comparison. Inference limited to at most one API call. | Trained legacy system, not general instruction-following models. | Tune overcalling and call thresholds against final outcome, not syntax alone. | Yes | **Retain, qualified** |

## Missing legacy material dimensions

The following legacy dimensions have no equivalent currently supported retention unit and must be explicitly restored or reported as gaps:

1. **Few-shot CoT task/scale boundary:** PaLM-540B GSM8K **56.9% versus 17.9%**, plus MAWPS SingleOp **94.1% versus 94.1%**. No live unit independently supports this direct CoT-versus-standard-prompt result.
2. **ReAct prompt-causal ambiguity and repeated-context token burden:** Song et al.’s ALFWorld ablation, including approximately **14M input** and **150K output tokens** over 134 instances. Current ReAct units establish benefits and failures, but not this prompt-sensitivity or cost dimension.
3. **Reflexion’s feedback-conditioned ablation:** GPT-4 Rust pass@1 **60.0% baseline**, **68.0% Reflexion**, and **52%** compromised feedback-free condition. FeedbackEval and self-verification evidence support related repair guidance but are not an equivalent intervention/comparator/result.

**Gate result:** retain the qualified units above, correct U11 before synthesis, and do not claim complete coverage of legacy CoT, ReAct-brittleness, or Reflexion-ablation dimensions without restored primary-source support.
